mainTopic: Why both wives do חליצה; רבא on a גט cancelling a מאמר; the two-sisters משנה and whether one איסור takes effect on top of another
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why both wives of one household do חליצה. If one wife had יבום and the other חליצה, a man might do חליצה first and then יבום, and the תורה forbids building a house he already refused to build. רבא then rules on a גט given to cancel a מאמר. In one version only the צרה becomes permitted. In another, even the woman herself is permitted, because the גט wipes out the מאמר. A new משנה teaches that if two brothers married two sisters and one brother died, his widow is forbidden forever, since she was forbidden for one moment as אחות אשה. The גמרא explains why this משנה is needed even though it seems obvious: it was taught first and was never moved. A ברייתא then brings a dispute between רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון about which איסורים he breaks if he lives with her. The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's view by the order of the marriages and רב אשי's idea of a suspended איסור. It then challenges whether רבי יוסי really holds that one איסור can take effect on top of another, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the worry: part of the house released by חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes stating its reason for requiring חליצה: people might think one household can be partly taken in יבום and partly released with חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and part of it is released by חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a sentence that began earlier. The גמרא is explaining that people might mistakenly say one household of wives can be split: one wife gets יבום and the other gets חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full worry is that people will see one wife taken in יבום and the other released with חליצה, and conclude that splitting a house is normal. To prevent that impression, the חכמים required both women to do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of it (part of the household)
The ceremony that releases a widow from the obligation of יבום
Levirate marriage, where a brother marries his childless brother's widow

phrases.english: and part of it is released by chalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning from the previous part of the daf explaining why the wives do חליצה rather than יבום.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both do חליצה so people will not think one household can be split between יבום and חליצה.

steps.title: So what if people say that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the worry: even if people did think a household could be split, what harm would it cause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason it just gave. If people mistakenly think one wife can have יבום and the other חליצה, why is that a problem?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing חליצה is never a sin in itself. So the challenge is that this mistaken idea seems harmless, and a decree to prevent it looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: So let them say it! (meaning: what harm would it do?)

phrases.english: So let them say it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The worry that people will say a household can be partly יבום and partly חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mistaken idea leads to no forbidden act, so there is no reason to make a decree against it.

steps.title: יבום first, then חליצה, would really be fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that if the brother did יבום with one wife first and then חליצה with the other, nothing would be wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does יבום and then afterward does חליצה, indeed there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by admitting part of the challenge. In one order, יבום first and then חליצה, splitting the house really would cause no harm. This sets up the real concern that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא grants that the challenge is right about one order of events. This narrows the problem down: the danger must come from the opposite order.

phrases.english: If he does yibum and then does chalitza,
indeed, so it is (there is no problem).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דִּמְיַיבֵּם וַהֲדַר חָלֵיץ הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Partly accepts the challenge of step 2 before giving the real answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession that narrows the concern to one order of events
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Splitting a household between יבום and חליצה is harmless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is harmless only when יבום comes first; the real answer follows in step 4.

steps.title: The real danger: חליצה first, then יבום
steps.stepSummary: The decree exists because a man might do חליצה with one wife first and then יבום with the other, which the תורה forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a decree, because he might first do חליצה and then do יבום. He would then fall under the פסוק 'who does not build', and the תורה says: once he did not build, he may not build again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer. The חכמים made a גזירה because someone might do חליצה with one wife first and then יבום with the other, and that is a real sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a brother does חליצה, he has chosen 'not to build' his brother's house, and the פסוק teaches that he can never build it afterward. So a mixed household could lead people to do יבום after חליצה. To block that, both women must do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree of the חכמים
'Who does not build' (the פסוק about חליצה)

steps.whatToRemember: The decree requiring חליצה for both wives is not about the חליצה itself. It is to stop anyone from doing יבום after a חליצה, because once a brother did not build his brother's house, he may never build it.
steps.confusionAlert: The order matters. יבום followed by חליצה is fine. חליצה followed by יבום is forbidden by the תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic rule that חליצה with one wife closes the door on יבום with any wife of that house.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a decree, lest he do chalitza first
and then do yibum,
and he stands in violation of "who does not build,"
and the Merciful One said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא בָּנָה — שׁוּב לֹא יִבְנֶה.
phrases.english: once he did not build, he may not build again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּזֵירָה דִּילְמָא חָלֵיץ בְּרֵישָׁא וַהֲדַר מְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer after the concession in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the true danger behind the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mistaken idea of a split household seems harmless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It could lead to יבום after חליצה, which the תורה forbids, so both wives do חליצה.

steps.title: A גט that cancels the מאמר frees the צרה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the brother gave a גט to cancel his מאמר, the other wife (the צרה) becomes permitted, but the woman who got the גט stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he gave a גט for his מאמר, her צרה becomes permitted. But she herself is forbidden, because people would confuse her with a woman who received a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new ruling about the case of the משנה. If the brother who did מאמר cancelled it with a גט, the other wife of the house is no longer blocked, but the woman who got the גט herself is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט undoes the bond of the מאמר. Her צרה is then no longer the rival of a woman tied to the house in two ways (her original זיקה plus the מאמר), so she may now have יבום. The woman who received the גט stays forbidden only as a precaution. Normally a יבמה who gets a גט may not have יבום, and permitting her here could confuse people about that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה, done before יבום
Her rival wife (another wife of the same husband)
Because she could be confused with

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a גט cancelling the מאמר frees the צרה, but the woman who got the גט stays forbidden so people will not confuse her with an ordinary divorced יבמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a גט can remove the legal tie created by מאמר, while the חכמים still guard against public confusion.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he gave a get for his ma'amar,
phrases.notes: He means the brother who did מאמר in the משנה's case gave a גט to cancel it.

phrases.english: her rival wife is permitted.
But she herself is forbidden,
because she could be confused with a woman who received a get.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ruling about the case of the משנה: what happens if the מאמר was cancelled with a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט cancelling the מאמר permits the צרה, but the woman who received the גט remains forbidden because of possible confusion with an ordinary divorced יבמה.

steps.title: A second version of רבא's ruling: the גט permits even her
steps.stepSummary: According to another version, רבא rules that a גט cancelling the מאמר permits even the woman who received it, because it wipes out what he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא actually said: if he gave a גט to cancel his מאמר, even she becomes permitted. Why? Whatever he did with her, the גט took it away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רבא's ruling from Step 5. In this version, even the woman who got the גט is permitted, not only the צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the גט freed the צרה but left the woman herself forbidden. Here, רבא holds that the גט fully cancels the מאמר. So it is as if he never did anything with her at all, and she goes back to her original status.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic kind of betrothal done by the brother-in-law before יבום
He took it away (it was cancelled)

phrases.english: There are those who say:
רבא said:
If he gave a bill of divorce for his מאמר,
even she is permitted.
phrases.notes: "Even she" means the woman who got the גט, not only the צרה from Step 5.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Whatever he did with her, he took away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's ruling from Step 5, with a more lenient result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given to cancel a מאמר wipes out the מאמר entirely, so even the woman herself is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבא. In the first, only the צרה is permitted. In the second, even she is permitted, because the גט erases the מאמר.

steps.title: New משנה: forbidden for one moment means forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: Two brothers married two sisters. One brother died, and then the other brother's wife died. The widow stays forbidden to him forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two brothers are married to two sisters. One brother dies, and later the second brother's wife dies. The widow is forbidden to him forever, since she was forbidden to him for one moment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. When the first brother died, his widow was the living sister of the surviving brother's wife, so she was forbidden to him. Even after his wife dies, she stays forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of death, the widow could not do יבום because of אחות אשה. Since the יבום obligation was blocked at that moment, it never comes back. The rule is that one moment of being forbidden makes her forbidden forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Since she was forbidden for one moment
A wife's sister, a woman forbidden by the תורה

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Two brothers married to two sisters,
and one of them died,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: and afterward the wife of the second one died,
this one is forbidden to him forever,
since she was forbidden to him for one moment.
phrases.notes: That moment was when her husband died while her sister, his brother's wife, was still alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁנֵי אַחִין נְשׂוּאִין שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving on from רבא's rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה who was forbidden to the brother-in-law even for a moment, as his wife's sister, stays forbidden to him forever.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear statement of the principle that one moment of being forbidden cancels the יבום obligation permanently. The rest of the sugya builds on it.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious from the earlier cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה is needed. If she was forbidden in the earlier cases, where a third brother kept her tied to the family, she should surely be forbidden here.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! In the earlier case, she was not completely pushed out of this family, and you still said she can't do יבום. Here she is completely pushed out, so surely she can't!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה as unnecessary, using a קל וחומר from the earlier משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases there was a third brother, so the woman still had a link to the family, and she was still forbidden. Here there are only two brothers, so she is cut off from the family completely. If the milder case was forbidden, the stronger case must be forbidden too. So why say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (why do we need to be told?)

phrases.english: GEMARA: It's obvious!
Now, if there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the earlier משניות, where there was a third brother.

phrases.english: where she is not completely pushed out of this household,
you said no,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא דְּקָא מִידַּחְיָא מֵהַאי בֵּיתָא לִגְמָרֵי
phrases.english: here, where she is completely pushed out of this household,
is it not all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה from Step 7 as already obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה in Step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the earlier, milder case was forbidden, so this stronger case obviously is too, and the משנה adds nothing.

steps.title: This משנה was written first and never moved
steps.stepSummary: The תנא taught this משנה first. Back then, he held the earlier cases were permitted. Later he changed his mind, but this משנה stayed where it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא taught this case first. At that time he saw the other cases as permitted and allowed them. Later he decided they were forbidden. Since that new ruling was dear to him, he put it first. And a משנה does not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this משנה only looks unnecessary because of a change in the תנא's view over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, the תנא held that only this case, with two brothers, was forbidden. That made this משנה necessary. Later he decided the three-brother cases were forbidden too. He placed that new ruling earlier because he loved it. Once a משנה has been taught, it is not removed, so this one stayed even though it is now obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: A משנה does not move from its place: once taught, it is not taken out

steps.confusionAlert: Watch out for "this one" and "that one" in this step. "This one" (הָא) is our משנה about two brothers. "That one" (הָךְ) is the earlier cases with a third brother, which were placed before it.

phrases.english: The תנא taught this one first,
and that one he saw as permitted, and he permitted it,
and then he saw it as forbidden.
And since it was dear to him, he placed it first,
phrases.notes: "It" is the new ruling forbidding the third-brother cases. That's why it appears earlier in the פרק.

phrases.english: and a משנה does not move from its place.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical explanation of how the משנה was put together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems pointless, since a קל וחומר from the earlier cases already teaches it.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was needed when first taught, before the תנא forbade the earlier cases. It remains because a משנה is never removed.
steps.whatToRemember: A משנה that looks obvious may come from an earlier stage of the תנא's thinking. Once taught, a משנה is not removed.

steps.title: ברייתא: which איסורים he breaks by living with her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says he is liable for both אשת אח and אחות אשה. רבי שמעון says only for אשת אח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if he lived with her, he is liable both for his brother's wife and for his wife's sister, says רבי יוסי. רבי שמעון says he is liable only for his brother's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the woman in our משנה. It asks which prohibitions the brother violates if he lives with her anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since יבום never became a מצוה for her, she remains his brother's wife. While his own wife is alive, she is also his wife's sister. רבי יוסי counts both איסורים, but רבי שמעון counts only one, אשת אח.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother's wife, forbidden by the תורה unless there is a מצוה of יבום

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he had relations with her,
phrases.notes: "Her" is the widow from our משנה. This has to be while his own wife, her sister, is still alive, because only then is she forbidden as his wife's sister.

phrases.english: he is liable for her because of brother's wife,
and because of wife's sister,
these are the words of רבי יוסי.
רבי שמעון says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָח בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: He is liable only because of brother's wife alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why the משנה was taught to the punishment for violating its איסור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: liable for both אשת אח and אחות אשה. רבי שמעון: liable only for אשת אח.

steps.title: Contradiction: another ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון as saying he is liable only for אחות אשה, which contradicts the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught elsewhere: רבי שמעון says he is liable only because of his wife's sister!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two ברייתות report opposite opinions in the name of רבי שמעון. It sets up the need for an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that רבי שמעון counts only one איסור. They disagree on which one. One says אשת אח, the other says אחות אשה, so the גמרא must explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught? Introduces a contradicting ברייתא

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
רבי שמעון says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה בִּלְבָד!
phrases.english: He is liable only because of wife's sister alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how Step 10 reports רבי שמעון's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's position as quoted in the ברייתא of Step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות quote רבי שמעון with opposite answers about which single איסור applies, so the גמרא needs to reconcile them.

steps.title: Which prohibition came first decides it
steps.stepSummary: The two quotes of רבי שמעון are about two different cases. In each case, the prohibition that came first is the only one that counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: No contradiction. One ברייתא is where the living brother married first and then the dead brother married. The other is where the dead brother married first and then the living brother married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 11. It says each ברייתא is talking about a different order of marriages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that once one prohibition is in place, a second one cannot add on top of it. If the living brother married first, she was already his wife's sister before she became his brother's wife, so only אחות אשה counts. If the dead brother married first, she was already his brother's wife, so only אשת אח counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
The dead one (the brother who died)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that for רבי שמעון the order of events decides which prohibition applies.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, where the living one married first,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא where רבי שמעון says only אחות אשה, because that prohibition came first.

phrases.english: and afterward the dead one married.
There, where the dead one married first,
and afterward the living one married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source deals with a different order of marriages.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to quote רבי שמעון saying opposite things about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They describe different cases. For רבי שמעון, whichever prohibition came first is the one that applies.

steps.title: Then why can't she do יבום?
steps.stepSummary: If only אשת אח applies when the dead brother married first, and יבום pushes aside אשת אח, she should be allowed to do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, where the dead brother married first and then the living brother married, the wife's-sister prohibition never took effect. So she should be allowed to do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's view. If only אשת אח is in place, nothing should stop יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of יבום normally overrides אשת אח. Step 12 said that in this case אחות אשה never took effect, so the only thing standing in the way is gone once יבום applies. Yet the משנה says she is forbidden, so how does רבי שמעון explain that?

phrases.english: And according to רבי שמעון,
where the dead one married first
and afterward the living one married,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיסּוּר אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה לָא חָיֵיל
phrases.english: since the prohibition of a wife's sister never took effect
she should be able to do יבום!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הֵיכָא דְּנָשָׂא מֵת וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָשָׂא חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks a result of the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that only אשת אח applies when the dead brother married first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום overrides אשת אח. If אחות אשה never took effect, she should be permitted for יבום, but the משנה forbids her.

steps.title: The second prohibition is waiting to take effect
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that אחות אשה is hanging in suspension. As soon as אשת אח falls away, אחות אשה steps in, so she never becomes permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wife's-sister prohibition stays hanging. If the brother's-wife prohibition falls away, the wife's-sister prohibition comes and takes effect. So she never becomes permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge from step 13. He says the second prohibition was never gone. It was waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחות אשה did not take effect at first only because אשת אח was already there. It was not cancelled. The moment יבום removes אשת אח, there is room for אחות אשה, and it takes hold right away, so she stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It stays hanging; it is suspended, waiting

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אחות אשה was cancelled. It just couldn't take effect yet because the other prohibition was already in place.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, a blocked prohibition is not erased. It waits and takes effect as soon as the first prohibition is removed.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The prohibition of a wife's sister
stays hanging in suspension.
If the prohibition of a brother's wife falls away,
the prohibition of a wife's sister comes and takes effect,
and therefore it does not fall away.
phrases.notes: In plain terms: she is never left with no prohibition, so she can't do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִיסּוּר אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה מִיתְלָא תְּלֵי וְקָאֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conceptual clarification: the blocked prohibition is suspended, not cancelled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since אחות אשה never took effect, removing אשת אח would leave her permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: אחות אשה waits and takes effect the moment אשת אח falls away, so she stays forbidden.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי really let one prohibition add on top of another?
steps.stepSummary: Step 10 showed רבי יוסי holds both prohibitions apply. But a ברייתא has רבי יוסי saying a person is judged only by the first prohibition that applied, which suggests the second does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי hold that one prohibition takes effect on top of another? But a ברייתא teaches: someone who did a sin carrying two death penalties is judged with the harsher one. רבי יוסי says: he is judged by the first connection that came upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי יוסי and challenges his view from step 10 using a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 רבי יוסי made him liable for both אשת אח and אחות אשה, which means a second prohibition can take effect on top of the first. But in the ברייתא about two death penalties, רבי יוסי says only the first prohibition counts. That sounds like a second prohibition does not take effect, a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition takes effect on top of an existing prohibition
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא
He is judged with the harsher penalty
Connection; here, the prohibition that first linked her to him

phrases.english: And does רבי יוסי hold
that a prohibition takes effect on top of a prohibition?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: עָבַר עֲבֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת
phrases.english: One who committed a sin that carries two death penalties
is judged with the harsher one.
רבי יוסי says:
He is judged by the first connection
phrases.notes: 'Connection' here means the first prohibition that made her forbidden to him.

phrases.english: that came upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי שמעון to רבי יוסי's view from step 10 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling in step 10 that he is liable for both אשת אח and אחות אשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי judging only by the first prohibition, which implies a second prohibition does not take effect on top of the first.

steps.title: The ברייתא: Sentenced Only for the First Prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא behind the challenge. רבי יוסי says a man is sentenced by the first prohibition. If she was first his חמות, he is sentenced for חמותו. If she was first an אשת איש, he is sentenced for אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: In what case did רבי יוסי say a person is sentenced according to the first prohibition that applied to him? If she was his mother-in-law and then became a married woman, he is sentenced for his mother-in-law. If she was a married woman and then became his mother-in-law, he is sentenced for a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the actual ברייתא that powers the challenge from Step 15. It gives two examples of רבי יוסי's rule that only the first prohibition counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each example the same woman becomes forbidden in two ways, one after the other. רבי יוסי sentences the man only for whichever prohibition came first. This suggests the later prohibition never took hold, which contradicts Step 10, where רבי יוסי seemed to hold that both prohibitions apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a 'connection' or link of prohibition, the way a woman is bound to a man as forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The word זיקה here does not mean the יבום bond between a widow and her husband's brother. It just means the link of prohibition that connects this woman to the man.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the evidence for the קשיא. The גמרא will need to explain how רבי יוסי can say only the first prohibition counts and still hold, as Step 10 showed, that both apply.

phrases.english: And it is taught: In what case did Rabbi Yosei say
he is sentenced by the first connection that came upon him?
If she was his mother-in-law and then became a married woman —
he is sentenced for his mother-in-law.
If she was a married woman and then became his mother-in-law —
he is sentenced for a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נִידּוֹן בַּזִּיקָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה הַבָּאָה עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the actual ברייתא text behind the challenge raised in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from Step 10 that רבי יוסי holds both prohibitions take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the man is sentenced only for the first prohibition, it looks like רבי יוסי holds the second prohibition does not take effect at all.
